Subject: Staffing Assignment Approach for the Service Center

Overview
We are conducting a staffing review to ensure the service center allocates people efficiently across its help desks, counters, and departmental stations. Customers arrive at each station at predictable rates throughout the day, and our teams have different skills and working speeds depending on where they are assigned.

Situation
- The center operates multiple service stations with distinct demand patterns. Some stations experience steady, high-throughput activity; others handle more complex interactions with longer handling times.
- We have multiple types of staff with varying qualifications. Not all staff types can serve at every station due to training and scope-of-practice constraints.
- The same staff type may work at different speeds depending on the station’s processes and the nature of the customer request. Handling speed is recorded as average minutes per customer, while incoming demand is tracked as customers per hour.

Staffing Challenge
Our task is to deploy the available workforce across stations so that:
- Each station has enough qualified people to keep pace with incoming customers.
- Staff are not scheduled so tightly that they have no buffer for variability, follow-up work, breaks, and unexpected surges.
- Baseline coverage is maintained at all stations during operating hours.
- We respect training limitations and only assign staff where they are qualified.
- We do not exceed the total number of people available for each staff type.
- We control total hourly staffing cost.

Service Quality Policy
- Demand and capacity alignment: For each station, we will align average minutes per customer with hourly arrival volumes and ensure the combined capacity of the assigned team comfortably exceeds the expected inflow. This operational buffer is a practical safeguard against queue buildup and service delays.
- Utilization cap: Staff should not be occupied more than a defined fraction of their time. This cap preserves service quality by preventing chronic overload and allows room for natural variability and non-customer-facing tasks.
- Minimum coverage: Every station must have a baseline number of on-duty staff at all times for safety, visibility, and continuity of service.

Cost and Feasibility Considerations
- Hourly cost varies by staff type. We will factor this into assignments so that we meet service targets at the lowest total hourly cost, without compromising coverage and quality.
- Some station–staff combinations are off-limits due to qualifications and will be treated as not assignable.
- Where practical, faster, qualified staff will be prioritized at higher-volume stations, while specialized or slower staff will be allocated where their skills are best matched to the work and demand is less intense.
- If coverage and utilization targets cannot be met with the current workforce, we will highlight gaps and recommend actions (e.g., cross-training, overtime, or schedule adjustments).

Outcome
The result will be a station-by-station staffing plan that:
- Meets or exceeds demand with a built-in buffer,
- Keeps individual utilization within our policy,
- Respects minimum coverage and qualification limits, and
- Minimizes total hourly staffing cost.
